newsitem.title: UK: Marks & Spencer says no decision on mail order.
newsitem.headline: Marks & Spencer says no decision on mail order.

text.p: British high street retail chain Marks & Spencer Plc said on Monday it had not decided whether to expand its mail order operations after a report in the Times newspaper said trials were expected in the autumn.
"We have made no decision yet whether to expand our mail order operations," a spokeswoman for Marks & Spencer said.
She described the report in the Times as "speculative."
The Times said that the retail chain, one of the best known in Britain, was preparing to launch trials of a clothing mail order service in the autumn.
Marks & Spencer already has a small number of mail order operations covering wine, food hampers and flowers and also has a mail order operation for home furnishings.
Shares in the retailer were up 2-1/2 pence by 1113 GMT to 498-1/2 pence while mail order group GUS eased 4-1/2 pence to 649 pence, worried by the possible competition threat, analysts said.
